card: Makes btck_LogEntry an opaque handle in the libbitcoinkernel C interface, exposing fields via btck_log_entry_get_* accessor functions. A public struct layout made it impossible to add or change log metadata fields without breaking ABI compatibility for kernel consumers, unlike other kernel API handles. Fields are now converted lazily when read, and author benchmarks show no meaningful performance impact (delta between -2.5 ns and +5.4 ns per log statement).
changed_since_previous: Diff provided; matches the previous description.
evidence: Author note in description: 'This allows adding or changing fields without breaking the ABI, and is consistent with ~all other kernel objects. Follow-up to https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34374#discussion_r4207440088.'
Author microbenchmarks show negligible overhead: callback log statement duration shifts between −2.5 ns and +5.4 ns depending on how many fields are read.
problem: Exposing `btck_LogEntry` as a public C struct fixes its memory layout in the library ABI, preventing the addition or alteration of log fields without breaking backwards compatibility. It also deviates from almost all other libbitcoinkernel types, which use opaque handles.

risk.why: Mistakes are confined to libbitcoinkernel logging callback wrappers and getters, causing corrupted log fields or compilation issues for external kernel consumers.

summary: Replaces the public struct definition of `btck_LogEntry` in the libbitcoinkernel C API with an opaque handle and explicit getter functions (`btck_log_entry_get_*`). String fields are returned as non-owning `btck_StringView` structs rather than raw pointer and length pairs. Field values are extracted lazily upon access rather than eagerly converted before calling the registered logging callback.
